facts.raw_span: two weeks of fever
generalized weakness, vague abdominal pain, vomiting, headache, body aches, and moderate nasal bleeding
a 2×1 cm submandibular lymph node
hepatomegaly (7 cm below the costal margin)
urea 18.8 mmol/L
creatinine 141 µmol/L
ferritin >40 000 µg/L
pancytopenia: hemoglobin 6.4 g/dL, WBC 1.7×10^3/µL, ANC 0.9×10^3/µL, platelets 2×10^3/µL
bilateral subdural hemorrhages without midline shift
bilateral pleural effusion, extensive pulmonary consolidation, thrombosis of the celiac artery with splenic infarction, mild hepatomegaly, and massive splenomegaly with infarction
13% abnormal blastoid cells of medium size with fine nuclear chromatin, unevenly distributed coarse basophilic granules, and occasional bilobed nuclei
bone marrow aspirate was hypercellular with 26% immature metachromatic blasts

concepts.why: The patient's pancytopenia, abnormal blastoid cells, and hypercellular bone marrow aspirate with immature metachromatic blasts are consistent with AML.
The patient's elevated ferritin, pancytopenia, and histiocytes demonstrating erythrophagocytosis are consistent with HLH.
The patient's bilateral subdural hemorrhages, thrombosis of the celiac artery, and splenic infarction are consistent with DIC.
The patient's fever, generalized weakness, and extensive pulmonary consolidation are consistent with sepsis.
The patient's pancytopenia, thrombocytopenia, and microangiopathic hemolytic anemia are consistent with TTP.
The patient's fever, generalized weakness, and elevated ferritin are consistent with SLE.
The patient's lymphadenopathy, hepatomegaly, and abnormal lymphoid cells are consistent with lymphoma.
The patient's pancytopenia, abnormal blastoid cells, and hypercellular bone marrow aspirate with immature metachromatic blasts are consistent with MDS.

rationales.F01: Fever is a non-specific symptom that can be seen in many conditions, including infections and hematological disorders.
rationales.F03: Lymphadenopathy can be seen in lymphoma, hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis, and other conditions.
rationales.F07: Elevated ferritin levels are characteristic of hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis.
rationales.F08: Pancytopenia can be seen in bone marrow failure syndromes, including acute myeloid leukemia and myelodysplastic syndrome.
rationales.F10: Multi-organ involvement, including hepatosplenomegaly and pulmonary consolidation, can be seen in disseminated intravascular coagulation and other conditions.
rationales.F11: The presence of abnormal blastoid cells in the peripheral blood is characteristic of acute myeloid leukemia.
rationales.F12: The bone marrow aspirate showing immature metachromatic blasts is characteristic of acute myeloid leukemia.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's presentation with fever, hepatomegaly, splenomegaly, and significantly elevated ferritin levels, along with evidence of hemophagocytosis in the bone marrow, strongly supports Hemophagocytic Lymphohistiocytosis. While Acute Myeloid Leukemia is also a consideration due to the presence of blastoid cells and a hypercellular bone marrow with immature metachromatic blasts, the overall clinical picture and laboratory findings more closely align with Hemophagocytic Lymphohistiocytosis.
